title: Infinite geometric series

points.text: Condition for a geometric series to converge
Sum to infinity and its uses

bigPicture: When |r| < 1 the terms shrink so fast that adding infinitely many of them gives a finite total. This turns recurring decimals and bouncing balls into one formula.

keyIdeas.cue: When does an infinite geometric series converge?
keyIdeas.answer: Only when |r| < 1 (−1 < r < 1); then S_n approaches a limit as n → ∞.

keyIdeas.cue: Sum to infinity, and its uses?
keyIdeas.answer: S∞ = u₁/(1 − r), |r| < 1. Uses: recurring decimals as fractions, total distance in repeated-rebound problems, finding u₁ or r from a given S∞, or the range of x for which a series in x converges.

keyTerms.def: S_n does not approach a finite limit

misconceptions.wrong: S∞ exists for r = −1.5 because the terms alternate

misconceptions.right: Each rebound is travelled up and down: add 2 × the rebound series to the first drop.

practice.prompt: The series 1 + (x − 1) + (x − 1)² + … converges. (a) Find the possible values of x. (b) Find its sum when x = 1/2.
A geometric series has S∞ = 12 and u₁ = 4. Find r and u₃.
A ball is dropped from 10 m and each rebound reaches 70% of the previous height. Find the total distance travelled before it comes to rest.
solution: rebounds: 7 + 4.9 + … up and the same down

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: Convergence condition |r| < 1 must be stated when asked
